extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy and political theory; those studying Plato's Republic
extracted.subtask_description: Constructing and evaluating the foundations of a just city and the corresponding virtues in individuals, including education, class-structure, censorship of arts, and the four cardinal virtues (wisdom, courage, temperance, justice).

rubrics_metrics.name: State size and self-sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Let our city be accounted neither large nor small, but one and self-sufficing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow the State to increase only so far as is consistent with unity; the proper limit is growth compatible with maintaining the city's unity and self-sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and mobility of guardians' offspring
rubrics_metrics.description: Degrading the offspring of the guardians when inferior, and elevating into the rank of guardians the offspring of the lower classes, when naturally superior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citizens' roles should follow nature: promote or demote children according to natural fitness so that each individual is put to the use for which nature intended him.

rubrics_metrics.name: One person, one function (division of labour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual should be put to the use for which nature intended him, one to one work, and then every man would do his own business, and be one and not many.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justice in the city consists in each class and person performing their own role and not meddling in others' functions; avoid individuals combining incompatible roles (trader+warrior+legislator) as ruinous to the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of education and nurture
rubrics_metrics.description: Education, and nurture: If our citizens are well educated, and grow into sensible men, they will easily see their way through all these matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good nurture and education implant good constitutions; education is the chief means by which citizens acquire virtues and the capacity to legislate their own lesser rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve traditional music and gymnastic; forbid musical innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Music and gymnastic be preserved in their original form, and no innovation made... for any musical innovation is full of danger to the whole State, and ought to be prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain existing musical modes because changes in musical modes lead to changes in fundamental laws and, ultimately, to disorder in the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundations of guardianship in music and gymnastic
rubrics_metrics.description: Our guardians must lay the foundations of their fortress in music... at first sight amusements appear harmless but may introduce lawlessness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train youth in music and gymnastic to instill order; amusements must be regulated because they can subtly corrode manners and law-abidingness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Censor amusements to prevent moral and legal corrosion
rubrics_metrics.description: Little by little this spirit of licence, finding a home, imperceptibly penetrates into manners and customs; whence... it invades contracts between man and man, and from contracts goes on to laws and constitutions... ending at last by an overthrow of all rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because lawlessness in amusements spreads into social and legal life, guardians must be wary and restrict forms of amusement that encourage licence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid legislating minutiae; rely on good citizens' judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: There is, I think, small wisdom in legislating about such matters... when the young are to be silent before their elders... what garments or shoes are to be worn... I doubt if it is ever done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not overburden the law with trivial regulations; good citizens educated rightly will discover appropriate local customs and practices without heavy-handed legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave religious rites to the divine interpreter (Apollo)
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution of temples and sacrifices, and the entire service of gods, demigods, and heroes... are matters of which we are ignorant ourselves, and as founders of a city we should be unwise in trusting them to any interpreter but our ancestral deity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Founders should refrain from prescribing sacred rites; defer to religious tradition/authority for ordering temples, sacrifices, and rites for the dead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four cardinal virtues as criteria for a good State
rubrics_metrics.description: A rightly ordered State is wise and valiant and temperate and just.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the presence and proper location of wisdom, courage, temperance, and justice in the city's classes as diagnostic standards for the city's excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wisdom located in rulers (good counsel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Good counsel is clearly a kind of knowledge... Is there any knowledge in our recently-founded State which advises not about any particular thing but about the whole? It is the knowledge of the guardians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State is 'wise' insofar as its ruling class (guardians) possess knowledge about the whole and give good counsel; wisdom is the province of the smallest class—the rulers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courage as preservation of correct opinion about dangers
rubrics_metrics.description: The city will be courageous in virtue of a portion of herself which preserves under all circumstances that opinion about the nature of things to be feared and not to be feared in which our legislator educated them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courage is the indelible fixation of correct beliefs about what to fear, implanted by education—resistant to pleasures, pain, desire, and fear (illustrated by the dyeing analogy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperance as harmony and self-mastery
rubrics_metrics.description: Temperance is the ordering or controlling of certain pleasures and desires... temperance has more of the nature of harmony and symphony... the agreement of the naturally superior and inferior, as to the right to rule of either.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temperance consists in the whole city (and soul) being in agreement about who should rule; it is an overall harmony between classes and parts of the soul—self-mastery of the better part over the worse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice defined as each doing one's own work
rubrics_metrics.description: Justice was doing one’s own business, and not being a busybody... when the trader, the auxiliary, and the guardian each do their own business, that is justice, and will make the city just.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justice in the State (and by analogy in the individual) is the structural principle that preserves and sustains the other virtues: each class/person performs its natural function and refrains from meddling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence between city-structure and soul-structure
rubrics_metrics.description: We may assume that [the individual] has the same three principles and habits which there are in the State... and he may be rightly described in the same terms, because he is affected in the same manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate individual virtue by mapping the city's three classes to the soul's parts: reason (rulers), spirit (auxiliaries), appetite (producers); moral diagnosis requires examining this internal correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tripartite soul: rational, spirited, appetitive
rubrics_metrics.description: The rational principle of the soul... that which bids and attracts proceeds from passion and disease... we may finally determine that there are two principles... and what of passion, or spirit? Is it a third, or akin to one of the preceding?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand moral psychology by distinguishing the soul's parts—reason (rational), spirit (thumos), appetite (desires)—and use this framework to judge actions and education's effects.
